market_wrap.text: Nifty fell 0.63% to 25,228 and the Sensex lost about 500 points, with metals, IT and FMCG the weakest sectors and mid caps down nearly 1%; a dollar near a 19-month high and rising bets on a US Fed rate rise in December weighed on sentiment even as crude eased. Your stocks and ETFs fell 1.5%, mostly because silver and gold slid again; mutual-fund NAVs come in tonight.

reasons.reason: Silver fell over 3% on MCX and below $46 an ounce globally, its lowest in more than a year, while gold dropped about 2%, as the dollar hit a 19-month high and markets priced in a near-certain US Fed rate rise in December ahead of the Fed's meeting minutes. A firmer rupee pushed domestic prices down further.

Metal stocks were the worst sector today (Nifty Metal down about 2.5%) as copper hit a five-month low on a strong dollar, Fed rate-rise expectations, weak China data and doubts over AI-related demand. No company-specific news.

No company news found today. Capital-market stocks fell as a group (KFin was the biggest loser, CAMS and Nippon AMC also down about 3%) after SEBI's chairman reportedly said the regulator is reviewing margin-trading limits; this also gave back part of Tuesday's 2.9% jump.
